[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on nuclear organisation and nucleocytoplasmic traffic: chromatin architecture, mRNA processing, ribosome biogenesis and export of cargo through the nuclear pore. CTCF and the cohesin subunit SMC1A together define chromatin loop boundaries and insulate promoters from inappropriate enhancers, which is how genome folding is translated into transcriptional output; ADNP and ATF1 act on transcription, the latter as a CREB-family factor responding to cAMP signalling.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on the regulation of gene expression at the steps between transcription and protein turnover. Cyclin T2 partners CDK9 in the elongation kinase that releases paused RNA polymerase II, while cyclin C works within the Mediator kinase module that gates promoter engagement, and ARID4A and SP3 act on chromatin and promoter DNA to set which genes are read.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on the braking and tuning of growth-factor signalling as it feeds into transcription, a control layer whose loss produces overgrowth, cancer and neurodevelopmental disease. Two GTPase-activating proteins, RASA2 for Ras and ACAP2 for an Arf-family GTPase, terminate signalling at the membrane, while MAP3K2 relays kinase input downstream and sorting nexins SNX13 and SNX14 govern endosomal trafficking and receptor fate.

[untitled BTM module] The dominant theme here is nuclear RNA production and maturation: an RNA polymerase I subunit supports ribosomal RNA transcription, a small-subunit processome component participates in pre-rRNA processing toward ribosome assembly, a general transcription factor subunit assists RNA polymerase II promoter opening, a spliceosome-associated crooked-neck-like factor acts in pre-mRNA splicing, and a core exosome subunit provides 3' to 5' exoribonuclease-mediated RNA trimming and surveillance; loss of that exosome subunit causes cerebellar hypoplasia with spinal motor neuron degeneration. Together these activities set the cell's capacity for ribosome biogenesis and accurate mRNA output, and hence growth and protein synthesis.

only_in_confusable: [untitled BTM module] The dominant theme here is chromatin-based control of gene expression coupled to ubiquitin-dependent protein regulation. Polycomb components BMI1 and EED, the histone chaperone ANP32E, the chromatin remodeller SMARCA5 and the histone-binding MORF4L2 together repress or reposition nucleosomes at developmental and proliferation genes, keeping stem and progenitor identity stable and restraining tumour suppressor loci such as the CDKN2A region.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping brings together proteins that have in common little more than a shared place in interaction screens, yet several of them converge on mitotic and genome-maintenance functions. SSNA1 is a microtubule-associated protein that promotes filament branching and localises to centrosomes and the midbody, and RASSF7 is likewise a centrosomal Ras-association domain protein required for orderly spindle formation and mitotic entry.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on control of cell survival and proliferation decisions during tissue growth and differentiation. Two hubs stand out: the retinoblastoma protein RB1, which restrains the G1/S transition by holding E2F-dependent transcription in check and whose loss underlies retinoblastoma and many sporadic cancers, and BCL2L1, an anti-apoptotic member of the BCL2 family that guards mitochondrial outer membrane integrity and blocks cytochrome c release.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on the housekeeping machinery that keeps mitochondria energetically competent while proteins and metabolites are turned over. Two accessory subunits of respiratory complex I sit alongside the mitochondrial translation elongation factor TUFM, which delivers aminoacyl-tRNAs to the mitoribosome and so supplies the organelle-encoded core of the respiratory chain; PRELID1 participates in phospholipid transfer between mitochondrial membranes, and TMEM160 is an inner-membrane protein.

members: [untitled BTM module] These genes converge on receptor-proximal signalling that converts extracellular cues into changes in cell adhesion, migration and tissue remodelling. One arm is vascular and mesenchymal: endoglin acts as a TGF-beta superfamily co-receptor in endothelium, CCN2/CTGF and CRIM1 shape growth-factor availability in the matrix, and focal adhesion kinase with GAB1, PLCB1 and the Ral activator RGL1 relay integrin and growth-factor input to the cytoskeleton and to Ras-family GTPase output.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on myeloid and platelet function, where surface signalling is translated into changes in the actin cytoskeleton and in gene expression. The Src-family kinase LYN sits at the top of immunoreceptor and integrin signalling in leukocytes and platelets, setting both activating and inhibitory tone, while LST1 is an immune-cell transmembrane protein that shapes membrane protrusions and cell-cell contact.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark a perivascular stromal and endothelial compartment, the interface where capillaries meet connective tissue matrix. Secreted matrix components such as EFEMP1 (fibulin-3) and ECM2 organise the basement membrane and elastic fibre environment that keeps vessels and surrounding tissue mechanically coherent, while IL33 acts both as a nuclear factor in endothelium and, when released from damaged cells, as an alarmin that recruits type 2 immune responses.

[untitled BTM module] These genes outline an endothelial identity and blood-vessel morphogenesis programme, of the kind that distinguishes vascular endothelium and sets arterial versus venous character during angiogenic remodelling. Its output is a patent, correctly patterned vascular network: guidance receptors such as neuropilin-1 and the fibronectin leucine-rich repeat protein FLRT2 read angiogenic and adhesive cues, adhesion-family GPCRs enriched in endothelium (ADGRL4/ELTD1, ADGRL2) tune sprouting behaviour, and the soluble guanylate cyclase alpha subunit places nitric oxide-cGMP signalling and vessel tone in the same module.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark the megakaryocyte-platelet arm of haematopoiesis and the signalling that supports it. Platelet factor 4 is the archetypal alpha-granule chemokine released on platelet activation, junction plakoglobin anchors the cytoskeletal junctions and desmosomal-type adhesion used by these cells, and the G protein alpha-z subunit couples platelet ADP and adrenergic receptors to inhibition of adenylate cyclase, lowering cyclic AMP to permit aggregation.

only_in_confusable: [untitled BTM module] These genes mark the resident fibroblast and perivascular stromal compartment of connective tissue, the cell population that builds and remodels extracellular matrix and supplies growth signals to neighbouring epithelium, endothelium and immune cells. Matrix and matrix-associated products such as tenascin C, ECM2, OLFML3 and the BMP antagonist chordin-like 1 shape tissue architecture and the diffusion of morphogens, while locally produced complement components C1S and C7 give stroma a role in innate immune surveillance.

[untitled BTM module] These genes read as the secretory programme of a mesenchymal stromal or fibroblast-like cell that builds and maintains tissue architecture and supports the cells embedded in it. CXCL12 is the chemokine by which such stroma recruits and retains haematopoietic progenitors and lymphocytes, while IGF1 with its carrier IGFBP3 sets local growth-factor availability, FRZB tunes Wnt signalling as a secreted antagonist, and complement component C7 and the secreted nuclease DNASE1L3 contribute to clearance of extracellular debris and immune tone.
